note: Aggregate published facts transcribed by Opus 5.5 from public Cambridge Core reader pages and their table images on 2026-11-05. No original asset is needed for the default replay; hashes allow an optional audit with --sources DIRECTORY.

target.citation: van Can JGP, van Loon LJC, Brouns F, Blaak EE. Reduced glycaemic and insulinaemic responses following trehalose and isomaltulose ingestion: implications for postprandial substrate use in impaired glucose-tolerant subjects. Br J Nutr 2012;108:1210-1217.
target.design: randomised single-blind crossover; ten overweight IGT subjects (6 men, 4 women) each 'studied four times' (GLUC, TRE, SUC, IMU), 1-week washout; on each trial day the same sugar drink was taken after an overnight fast (breakfast, 08.45) and again with a standardised mixed lunch (12.30)
target.all_four_conditions_verified: Methods: 'Each subject participated in four trials'; Abstract: 'ten overweight IGT subjects were studied four times'
target.dose_text: 'The CHO load consisted of 75 g CHO equivalents and was dissolved in 400 ml of water'; lunch: '25 En% of the total energy content of the meal was provided in the form of a beverage containing either TRE, IMU, GLUC or SUC'
target.dose_ambiguity: Whether the lunch beverage was 75 g or 25 En% of an individualised lunch is not reconciled in the text; the mass basis of 'CHO equivalents' for trehalose and isomaltulose (anhydrous vs hydrate) is not stated
target.sampling: venous, t = -5 (baseline), 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180 min after ingestion; no 15 or 45 min samples
target.operator: 'incremental area under the curve (iAUC) ... calculated by the trapezoid method'; handling of area below baseline not stated
target.statistics: paired t-tests only within GLUC v. TRE and SUC v. IMU; 'The four CHO were not compared with each other'
target.conversion_printed: To convert insulin from uU/ml to pmol/l, multiply by 6
target.dispersion: Tables 2 and 3 print means only (no SE)

insulin_iAUC_0_180.locator: Table 2 (TRE v. GLUC) and Table 3 (IMU v. SUC), Insulin row

lunch_TRE_v_GLUC.source: Results text 'but not when TRE was ingested with a mixed meal'; Table 2 no mark

target.figure_status: Fig. 1 GIF renders with a transparent background so axes and labels are not visible; group-curve values were not read

donors_2009.common_protocol: same laboratory; 75 g CHO (equivalents) in 400 ml water after an overnight fast (08.40); repeated the same day with a standardised lunch (12.30) in which '25 % energy of the total energy content of the meal was provided in the form of a beverage'; samples t = -5, 30 ... 180 min; plasma insulin RIA (LINCO); 'incremental area under the curve (minus baseline values, change in area under the curve)' by trapezoid; paired t-tests

trehalose.citation: van Can JGP, IJzerman TH, van Loon LJC, Brouns F, Blaak EE. Reduced glycaemic and insulinaemic responses following trehalose ingestion: implications for postprandial substrate use. Br J Nutr 2009;102:1395-1399.
